Rashi on Pesachim 79a:10:1.hebrew: יותרת הכבד ושתי הכליות מנא לן - מדאיצטריך ליה למיתני מנחה לא הויא שיור, מכלל דסבירא ליה דהני, דגופיה דזבח נינהו, הוי שיור:
Rashi on Pesachim 79a:10:1.english: The diaphragm and the two kidneys, from where do we [know this]? - Since it was necessary for him to teach [that] a meal-offering is not a remainder, it follows by implication that he holds that these, which are of the body of the sacrifice itself, are a remainder.

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:11:1.hebrew: אמר קרא - בהאי קרא גופיה, "והקטיר החלב לריח ניחוח":
Rashi on Pesachim 79a:11:1.english: The verse states - In this very verse [it states]: "And he shall burn the fat for a pleasing aroma."

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:13:1.hebrew: יעשו בטומאה - ואפי' טמאין יחידין, דהא פסח דטהורין גופיה בטומאה אתי משום כהנים:
Rashi on Pesachim 79a:13:1.english: They should perform [it] in ritual impurity - And even [the] individual impure [people], for the Paschal [offering] of the pure [people] itself comes in ritual impurity because of the priests.

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:14:1.hebrew: שאין קרבן צבור - הבא בטומאה חלוק. מאחר שקרבן רובן בא בטומאה, אף היחיד עושה בטומאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 79a:14:1.english: For a communal offering is not - [that which] comes in impurity, divided. Since the offering of the majority comes in impurity, the individual also performs [his offering] in impurity.

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:15:1.english: They only taught [this] - which implies [that] because of the impurity of service vessels, they all perform [the service] in [a state of] impurity.

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:15:2.hebrew: אלא שנטמא סכין בטמא מת - שהוא אב הטומאה, דנעשה אף הסכין אב הטומאה לטמא אדם:
Rashi on Pesachim 79a:15:2.english: Only where a knife became impure through one who is impure from a corpse - For he is a primary source of impurity, so that the knife also becomes a primary source of impurity to render a person impure.

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:15:3.english: For the Merciful One said, "by one slain with a sword" - To expound from it that a metal vessel that becomes impure through [contact with] a corpse becomes like that which it touched.

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:18:1.hebrew: טומאה דחויה היא בצבור - בקושי הותרה, וכל כמה דאפשר לאהדורי אטהרה או אטומאה קלה, מהדרינן:
Rashi on Pesachim 79a:18:1.english: Impurity is overridden in [cases involving] the public - It was permitted [only] with difficulty, and as much as it is possible to strive for purity or for a lighter [degree of] impurity, we strive [to do so].

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:1:1.english: If you wish, say Rav, who said - [That] if one sprinkled [the blood], it is accepted.

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:1:2.english: Like Rabbi Yehoshua - Who holds [that] eating the Paschal offerings is not essential.

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:20:1.english: We apply to it: “the flesh, every one that is pure may eat flesh” - And not an impure [person].

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:22:1.hebrew: הללו עושין לעצמן - בטהרה, והללו עושין לעצמן בטומאה. טהורים לא עבדי בטומאה, דהוי כרוב, ורוב טהורין לא עבדי בטומאה; וטמאין לשני לא מידחו, משום דהוו נמי רובא, ורובא לשני לא מידחו:
Rashi on Pesachim 79a:22:1.english: These perform [it] for themselves - In [a state of] purity, and those perform [it] for themselves in [a state of] impurity. [The] pure ones do not perform [it] in impurity, because they are like a majority, and a majority of pure people do not perform [it] in impurity; and [the] impure ones are not deferred to the second [Pesach], because they too are a majority, and a majority is not deferred to the second [Pesach].

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:22:2.hebrew: טהורין עושין הראשון - בטהרה, דאי נמי מיעוטא נינהו אית להו למעבד הראשון בטומאה, וכל שכן כי עבדי בטהרה שפיר דמי:
Rashi on Pesachim 79a:22:2.english: [Those who are] pure perform the first - in [a state of] purity; for even if they are a minority, they are to perform the first [Passover] in impurity, and all the more so when they perform [it] in purity, it is proper.

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:22:3.hebrew: וטמאין עושין את השני - דכיון דאינן כרוב, נידונין כמיעוט ונידחין לשני:
Rashi on Pesachim 79a:22:3.english: And [those who are] impure perform [the offering on] the second [Pesach] - For since they are not like a majority, they are judged as a minority and are deferred to the second [Pesach].

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:2:1.hebrew: שלמי נזיר - תחילתן לאכילה, דבעי שילוח שערו תחת הדוד שהשלמים מתבשלין בו, כדכתיב (במדבר ו׳:י״ח) "ולקח את שער ראש נזרו ונתן על האש" וגו'. ועוד, בעי תנופה זרוע בשלה. אלמא, צריך שיהא בשר טהור בשעת זריקה, שיהא ראוי למצוה האמורה בו:
Rashi on Pesachim 79a:2:1.english: The peace-offerings of a nazirite - Their primary purpose is for eating, as it requires casting his hair under the pot in which the peace-offerings are cooked, as it is written (Numbers 6:18): "And he shall take the hair of his consecrated head, and put it on the fire, etc." And furthermore, it requires waving of the boiled shoulder. Thus, it is necessary that the meat be pure at the time of sprinkling [the blood], so that it will be fit for the mitzvah stated regarding it.

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:2:2.english: And if he sprinkled [the blood], it was accepted - For these do not prevent [its acceptance].

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:3:1.hebrew: נטמאו בעלים - במת, דלא חזו למיכל לאורתא, דטומאתן שבעה:
Rashi on Pesachim 79a:3:1.english: The owners became ritually impure - from a corpse, since they are not fit to eat [it] in the evening, for their impurity is seven [days].

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:3:2.hebrew: ואם זרק לא הורצה - דאע"ג דאכילתו לא מעכבא, גברא דחזי לאכילה בעינן, ורחמנא דחייה לטמא נפש לפסח שני. ובנזיר נמי כתיב (שם) כי ימות מת עליו וגו', דסותר את נזירותו:
Rashi on Pesachim 79a:3:2.english: And if one sprinkled [it], it was not accepted - Even though eating it is not indispensable, we require a person who is fit for eating [it], and the Merciful One deferred one who is ritually impure from a corpse to the Second Pesach. And regarding a nazirite as well, it is written (there), "If a person dies beside him, etc.," [teaching] that it voids his naziriteship.

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:5:1.english: Half an olive-bulk of meat and half an olive-bulk of fat, [one] does not sprinkle the blood - For human consumption and altar consumption do not combine.

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:6:1.hebrew: אפי' כולה קיימת לא יזרוק - את הדם עליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 79a:6:1.english: Even [if] all of it remains, one may not sprinkle - the blood on account of it.

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:7:1.english: What is a meal-offering doing - with the sprinkling of blood?

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:7:2.hebrew: מנחת נסכים - הבאה עם הזבח. מהו דתימא, כזבח דמיא ותיהוי במקום זבח להכשיר את הדם:
Rashi on Pesachim 79a:7:2.english: The meal-offering of libations - That comes with the offering. What might you have thought? [That] it is like the offering, and would stand in place of the offering to render the blood fit [for sprinkling].

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:8:1.english: From where do we [derive] fat - That it is a remainder to validate the sprinkling of the blood.

Rashi on Pesachim 79a:8:2.hebrew: והקטיר החלב - גבי זריקת דם כתיב, דכתיב וזרק הכהן את הדם וגו' עד והקטיר החלב לריח ניחוח:
Rashi on Pesachim 79a:8:2.english: And he shall make the fat smoke - [This] is written regarding the sprinkling of blood, as it is written: "And the priest shall sprinkle the blood, etc." until "and he shall make the fat smoke for a satisfying aroma."

Tosafot on Pesachim 79a:13:1.hebrew: או שהיו כהנים טמאים יעשו בטומאה - אע"פ שיכולין ליזהר שלא יגעו בבשר, כיון דאישתראי טומאת אימורים אישתראי נמי טומאת בשר; דאמר במי שהיה טמא (לקמן פסחים דף צו.): "כל היכא דאישתראי טומאת בשר אישתראי טומאת אימורים" — משמע שהם שוים:
Tosafot on Pesachim 79a:13:1.english: "Or if the priests were impure, they shall perform [it] in impurity" - Even though they can be careful not to touch the meat, since the impurity of the sacrificial parts [eimurim] was permitted, the impurity of the meat was also permitted; as it says in [the chapter] Mi Shehayah Tamei (below, Pesachim 96a): "Wherever the impurity of the meat was permitted, the impurity of the sacrificial parts was permitted" — [which] implies that they are equal.

Tosafot on Pesachim 79a:15:1.hebrew: אלא שנטמא סכין בטמא מת כו' - תימה: א"כ מאי "אפי'" דקאמר? היינו רישא ממש — "היו ישראל טהורים וכהנים וכלי שרת טמאים" — כיון דמיטמא גברא מחמת סכין:
Tosafot on Pesachim 79a:15:1.english: "Only where the knife became impure through [contact with] one impure from a corpse, etc." - It is astonishing: if so, what is [the point of] "even" that [the baraita] says? This is literally the earlier clause — "[if] Israel were pure and the priests and sacred vessels were impure" — since the person [performing the service] becomes impure because of the knife:

Tosafot on Pesachim 79a:16:1.hebrew: בטומאת הגוף דבכרת מיתעביד - וא"ת: ישחוט בסכין ארוכה ולא יצטרך ליכנס לעזרה, אי נמי יאחוז הסכין בפשוטי כלי עץ וישחוט? ואומר ר"י, דאין פנאי לכל הפסחים לשחוט בענין זה, ואף להביא סכינים אחרים אין פנאי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 79a:16:1.english: It is performed in [a state of] ritual impurity of the body [that carries the penalty] of karet - And if you say: Let him slaughter with a long knife, and he will not need to enter the Temple Courtyard, or else let him hold the knife with flat wooden utensils [which do not contract impurity] and slaughter? And the Ri says that there is not [enough] time for all the Paschal lambs to be slaughtered in this manner, and even to bring other knives there is not [enough] time.

Tosafot on Pesachim 79a:2:1.hebrew: נזיר ועושה פסח נטמא בשר וחלב קיים אינו זורק כו' - ריב"א אומר דלא גרס "נזיר", דאין חילוק בזה בין נזיר לשאר קרבנות. ומה שפירש רש"י דבעי שילוח שערו תחת הדוד — אין נראה שיהא עיכוב; ומה שפי' נמי משום תנופה — הא כל שאר שלמים נמי בעו תנופה, ולא אשכחן תנא דאית ליה תנופה בנזיר מעכבת אלא ר"א בסוף ג' מינים (נזיר דף מו.). ובתוספתא לא גרס "נזיר":
Tosafot on Pesachim 79a:2:1.english: "A nazirite and one who performs [the ritual of] a Paschal lamb, [if] the meat became impure and the fat remains [pure], one does not sprinkle [the blood], etc." - Riba says that he does not read [the word] "nazirite" [in the text], for there is no distinction in this matter between a nazirite and other offerings. And as for what Rashi explained, that [the nazirite] requires casting his hair under the pot — it does not seem [correct] that this should be an indispensable requirement; and as for what he also explained, [that it is] because of the waving [of the offering] — behold, all other peace-offerings also require waving! And we do not find a Tanna who holds that waving in [the offering of] a nazirite is indispensable except Rabbi Eliezer at the end of [the chapter] Sheloshah Minim (Nazir 46a). And in the Tosefta, it does not read "nazirite":
